entries.english: Proceedings before the Imperial Chamber Court concerning the reversion of male fiefs. The plaintiff is Count Heinrich of Castell (Count Konrad of Castell was defendant in the first instance); the intervening defendants and agnatic fief heirs are the numerous named Lords von Heßberg, heirs of Gabriel von Heßberg of Weitersroda. The first-instance Castell fief court at Wiesenbronn held that, after Gabriel von Heßberg died as the last male descendant of Bernhard von Heßberg, the fiefs at Rödelsee, Prühl, and Fröhstockheim had reverted. The Heßberg agnates sought enfeoffment, arguing that the fief remained with a lineage until it became wholly extinct, whereas Castell relied on contrary imperial customs. Imperial commissions heard evidence in 1579 and 1582; in 1590 the Castell count’s house was ordered to grant the disputed properties and accrued revenues as fiefs. Both sides maintained their first-instance positions. The file contains the 1525 purchase charter for properties at Rödelsee, Fröhstockheim, Großlangheim, Prühl, Herpersdorf, Birkach auf der Heide, Mainstockheim, and Nenzenheim; the complete witness evidence and associated imperial commissions; fief documents for the many named castles, villages, tithes, and estates; legal opinions; and the 1676 printed *Notitia Actorum in causa Castell contra Heßberg Appellationis*. Witnesses include Konrad von Rosenberg, Georg Ludwig von Seinsheim, Veit Erasmus von Eyb, Christoph Truchseß von Pommersfelden, Joachim von Seckendorff, Hans Joachim Stiebar von Buttenheim, Hans Zobel von Giebelstadt, Valentin and Eyrich von Münster, Heinrich and Hans von Bibra, Hans Nikolaus and Christoph von Schaumberg, Wilhelm, Hans Christoph and Hans von Egloffstein, Georg von Heldritt, Lorenz von Guttenberg, Georg Marschall von Ebneth, Hektor von Rabenstein, and Joachim von Redwitz, among many others. Register: proceedings began in 1591. Previous courts: the fief court at Schleusingen and the fief court at Wiesenbronn.
